In this home-favorite, normal-rest, fair-weather spot Carolina is 1-1 ATS at home in three, 1-1 ATS as a favorite in three, 2-1 ATS on normal rest in four, and 2-2 ATS in five benign-weather games, and they covered last week at Philadelphia. Tampa Bay’s matching spots are softer: 1-1 ATS on the road in three, 2-3 ATS as a dog in six, 1-2 ATS on normal rest in four, and 1-3 ATS in five fair-weather games, with a non-cover last week against Pittsburgh after covers against Dallas and Green Bay. Head-to-head is empty. The line has moved from -3.5 to -2.5 toward Tampa Bay, but Tampa Bay is missing Luke Goedeke, Antoine Winfield Jr., and Emeka Egbuka, with Baker Mayfield questionable, while Carolina lists only Jaelan Phillips out. Lean Carolina at home.

Week 8 samples are still modest, but this spot is lopsided in the splits. Houston is 0-3 ATS at home in 4, 1-4 ATS as a favorite in 6, and 0-4 ATS indoors in 5, so a home favorite in a dome is the role that has not covered. The Giants are 3-1 ATS as a dog in 5, including a Week 6 road-dog cover at Washington, though they are only 1-1 ATS on the road in 3 and failed to cover as a 7.5-point road dog at the Rams in Week 3. No head-to-head is on file. The line has moved from -9.5 to -10.5 toward Houston, and New York is the thinner injury group, with Newsome and Holland out and Adebo and Nubin questionable, while Houston is without Montgomery and safeties Pitre and Blankenship. That move and the secondary absences are the caution; the graded pattern still points to the dog, so the lean is the Giants.

Minnesota is 4-1 ATS overall in 6 and 3-1 ATS as a favorite in 5, and four of the last five covers stuck, the miss coming at home laying 11.5. Indianapolis is 2-2 ATS as a dog in 5 and 1-2 ATS indoors in 4, against Minnesota's 2-1 indoor mark in 4, and the Colts have failed to cover their last two. The counter-crumbs are small and site-specific: Indianapolis is 2-1 ATS on the road in 4 and 1-0 ATS traveling one zone in 2, while Minnesota is only 1-1 ATS at home in 3 with a 0-0 bye split in 1. No head-to-head series and no line path are in the packet. Indianapolis is without Sauce Gardner, Tyler Warren, and Anthony Gould, with Justin Walley and Bryce Boettcher questionable, and Minnesota's injury list is empty. Samples are still early-season thin, but the favorite split, recent covers, and the injury gap lean Minnesota at home.

Week 8 samples are still thin, and the usable crumbs point in opposite directions. N.Y. Jets are 2-0 ATS at home in 3 and 1-0 ATS as a favorite in 2, inside a 4-2 ATS record in 7 and a 3-2 ATS mark on normal rest in 6, while Miami is 1-2 ATS on the road in 4 and 2-3 ATS as a dog in 6, with a bye split still 0-0 ATS in 1 and no head-to-head on file. The week-of indicators cut the other way: the Jets list Breece Hall, Dylan Parham, and Kene Nwangwu questionable against only Willie Gay Jr. questionable (illness) for Miami, and the line ran -4.5 to -5.5 before returning to -4.5. Both sides also covered their last two decided games, the Jets including a home-favorite cover and Miami both as a dog. The split record and the injury and line-path read do not line up, so this is a no-call.

Cleveland is 4-0 ATS in five benign-weather games and 3-0 ATS on four normal-rest weeks, while Tennessee is 1-2 ATS in four benign games and 1-2 ATS in four home games. Cleveland’s road body is the soft spot: 1-2 ATS in four away games, with the graded results all coming as a dog and the favorite split still 0-0 ATS in one. Tennessee is 3-2 ATS in six as a dog and 1-4 straight up in those games, and the only home cover in the last six weeks was a Week 3 win over Philadelphia. No head-to-head is listed. The home number has moved from +1.5 to +2.5, and Cleveland’s questionable corner and linebacker against one questionable Tennessee safety leave the weather and rest lean intact. Lean Cleveland.

Arizona is 0-2 ATS at home in three games, and both graded home spots were as a dog: they failed to cover against Detroit and Seattle. Their 3-2 ATS dog record in six games is a road profile (3-1 ATS away in four), so the home-dog role this week cuts against the split that has actually been working. Denver is 2-0 ATS as a favorite in three games, including a Week 6 road cover at the Chargers, though the full road body is only 1-2 ATS in four and one-zone trips are 1-2 ATS in four. Long rest is ungraded for Denver (0-0 in one), and indoor results do not separate them (Denver 1-0 ATS in two, Arizona 2-2 ATS in five). Arizona’s list is heavier, with Nolen, Gaines, Love, and Wingard out and Melton and Baker questionable, against Denver’s Hufanga out and Surtain and Coleman questionable. Six graded games is still a thin book, but the home failures and the favorite covers lean Denver.

Week 8 samples are still thin — Green Bay has six graded games and Detroit five — but Green Bay’s road record is enough to take a side. As a visitor Green Bay is 0-3 ATS in four games, and on one-zone trips they are 0-2 ATS in three; both of their covers came at home, against Dallas and Chicago, so that recent streak does not match this week’s site. Detroit is a flat 1-1 ATS at home in three and 2-2 ATS as a favorite in five, and the bye has no graded cover sample (0-0 in one), while Green Bay is 2-1 ATS on a normal week in four, so rest does not add a proven edge. The dome splits do: Detroit is 2-1 ATS indoors in four, Green Bay is 0-1 ATS indoors in two, and every injury is on Green Bay (Zaire Franklin out, Aaron Banks and Bo Melton questionable) with Detroit’s list empty.

Las Vegas is 5-1 ATS in 6 graded games, with the spots that match this game all pointing the same way: 3-0 at home in 4, 4-1 as a dog in 6, and 5-0 indoors in 6. On a normal week they are 4-1 ATS in 6, and the recent sheet is five covers in six, including home-dog wins against Buffalo and Kansas City. The Rams are 2-4 ATS as favorites in 7 games and 1-2 indoors in 4, with a road split of only 1-1 in 3 and a thin 1-0 on normal rest in 2; they have missed four of their last six as favorites and failed to cover each of the last two. The line moved from home +4.5 to +3 before settling at +3.5, so the market has come in on Las Vegas and only given a half-point back. There is no head-to-head sample. Nate Landman is out for the Rams, with Puka Nacua and Trent McDuffie questionable, against one Las Vegas questionable in Quay Walker. Lean Las Vegas at home.

Seattle is 0-3 ATS at home in 4 and 1-5 ATS as a favorite in 7, and has failed to cover as a favorite in 5 of 6 graded games. That shows up in the recent list: four straight non-covers, including home favorite spots against San Francisco and the Chargers, with the only cover in the last six coming Week 3 at Arizona. Kansas City is 3-2 ATS in 6, but the matching spots are thinner — 1-1 ATS on the road in 3, no graded result in their one game as a dog, and 0-1 ATS in 2 when traveling two time zones. Seattle’s long-rest split is the counter (1-0 ATS in 2 versus Kansas City 1-1 ATS in 3 on a normal week), and Kansas City is without Rashee Rice and tackle Jaylon Moore, with L’Jarius Sneed questionable, while Seattle’s list is Drake Thomas out plus three defensive questionables.

Philadelphia is 0-3 ATS at home in four games and 0-4 ATS in five benign-weather games, the two clearest graded splits in a week-8 packet that is still only six decided games deep. As a dog they are a thin 1-1 ATS in three, and the only recent cover was on the road; they have covered once in the last six. Dallas is 1-2 ATS on the road and 1-2 ATS as a favorite in four games each, with long-rest, one-zone, and benign marks all a thin 0-1 in two, so those fades exist but do not match Philadelphia's sample. Head-to-head and the line path are unknown. Philadelphia is also the more depleted side: DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out, with Saquon Barkley and Jonathan Greenard questionable, while Dallas is without Dee Winters and KaVontae Turpin. Home and fair-weather non-covers plus that injury gap lean Dallas.
